reuseRule: Original/later inventories retained; identical teaching reuses prior full reads after exact identity checks. Changed teaching and seven original-only units stay explicit.

interpretationRequirements.IND-002: Distinguish a functional mitochondrial challenge from protein abundance, allowing for shared survival roles and protocol-dependent responses.
interpretationRequirements.IND-007: Distinguish access through the cell boundary, the mitochondrial membranes and cytochrome-c release, and separate priming from intact-cell death and clinical benefit.
interpretationRequirements.IND-008: Explain which membrane is permeabilised for assay access and which mitochondrial event is being measured, separately from a cell-death endpoint.
interpretationRequirements.IND-010: Compare vehicle and drug pre-exposure under the same defined challenge; keep mitochondrial response, later cell death and clinical evidence separate.
interpretationRequirements.IND-029: Distinguish a printing plan from a built channel, cell health, fluid passage and measured barrier performance.
interpretationRequirements.IND-041: Evaluate the measured properties of a printed construct against the question it is intended to answer.
interpretationRequirements.IND-044: Explain how culture history can change biology and drug response under the same cell-line name.
interpretationRequirements.IND-048: Distinguish identity, contamination and phenotype checks; explain why passage number is not a universal count of divisions or biological drift.
interpretationRequirements.IND-059: Separate the intended identity of a culture from the history and selection shaping its current behaviour.
interpretationRequirements.IND-062: Attribute a mixed-culture signal to the populations that produced it, allowing their numbers and states to change.
interpretationRequirements.IND-067: Compare direct contact, a validated separating membrane and conditioned-medium transfer, then measure the contribution of each population.
interpretationRequirements.IND-078: Require population identity, origin and attributed measurements before interpreting a co-culture interaction.
interpretationRequirements.IND-081: Distinguish a genetic dependency from drug inhibition and safe treatment, including compensation and alternative protein forms.
interpretationRequirements.IND-086: Check editing, controls and copy-number cutting effects before attributing a genetic dependency; evaluate drug and clinical claims separately.
interpretationRequirements.IND-087: Interpret guide-read shares as relative representation, with copy-number cutting as a possible confounder, rather than counting dead cells.
interpretationRequirements.IND-099: Scope a dependency score to the genetic intervention, model and assay rather than treating it as a personal drug-response probability.
interpretationRequirements.IND-102: Distinguish a direct experiment in collected material from prediction of benefit, recognising omitted delivery, metabolism and toxicity.
interpretationRequirements.IND-109: Interpret a reduced bulk metabolic signal alongside unchanged identified tumour-cell endpoint counts; do not reconstruct death or division history from those endpoints alone.
interpretationRequirements.IND-120: Explain which local neighbours a fragment can retain and which circulation and recruitment processes it loses.
interpretationRequirements.IND-125: Connect viable fragment preparation and quality checks to attributed experimental response and a separately evaluated intended use.
interpretationRequirements.IND-126: Distinguish retained local anatomy from perfused delivery or recruitment of new immune cells, including diffusion limits in a cut slice.
interpretationRequirements.IND-133: Explain why retained tissue structure does not establish unchanged exposure, circulation or cell survival.
interpretationRequirements.IND-136: Distinguish experimental settings by their retained components and observations while allowing living preparations to change after removal.
interpretationRequirements.IND-147: Identify the measured or predicted object and omitted processes in each setting, without imposing a universal validation order or guaranteed clock.
interpretationRequirements.IND-152: Compare local immune retention with whole-host circulation and exposure, separately from the time and feasibility of an experiment.
interpretationRequirements.IND-155: Define trust by the intended job and supporting observations, allowing living models to adapt rather than ranking complexity alone.
interpretationRequirements.IND-161: Distinguish question, construction, measurement, prediction and proposed use as evidence questions rather than a mandatory universal sequence.
interpretationRequirements.IND-171: Scope a controlled-growth conclusion to sound identity, controls and readout while keeping clinical benefit unproven.
interpretationRequirements.IND-174: Distinguish a three-dimensional arrangement and selected tissue features from completeness of a patient or tumour.
interpretationRequirements.IND-175: Identify selection, retained and missing populations in an organoid; treat added cells as a new experiment requiring checks.
interpretationRequirements.IND-193: Attribute a measured response to verified retained cells and exposure while identifying missing immune interactions and clinical evidence.
interpretationRequirements.IND-196: Explain how implantation into another host changes selection and the tumour's surrounding compartments.
interpretationRequirements.IND-200: Separate graft establishment, feature validation and an interpretable experiment, with their own denominators and clocks.
interpretationRequirements.IND-204: Distinguish human tumour targets from mouse-derived support and verify species-specific binding required by a mechanism.
interpretationRequirements.IND-215: Identify source, host compartments, selection, passage, endpoint and denominator before interpreting a xenograft result.
interpretationRequirements.IND-218: Compare a xenograft, expanded organoid and tissue fragment as preparations retaining different parts of an ecosystem.
interpretationRequirements.IND-221: Compare selected human and mouse compartments, immune populations and circulation across the three models without making a universal hierarchy.
interpretationRequirements.IND-239: Evaluate a near-term decision using the required components, feasible clock and demonstrated function, without assuming a usable fragment or benefit from model-guided care.
interpretationRequirements.IND-242: Distinguish buoyant mass relative to displaced fluid from diameter, dry mass and cell divisions.
interpretationRequirements.IND-243: Interpret repeated mass measurements and rate units; a 75 percent reduction between two positive accumulation rates is not shrinkage, death or a patient response.
interpretationRequirements.IND-257: Distinguish mass at a moment, accumulation per time and evidence that identified cells died.
interpretationRequirements.IND-260: Distinguish the engineered design from the biological state measured after cells change their environment.
interpretationRequirements.IND-264: Choose and verify required chip components, local exposure, endpoints and matched controls before claiming a modelled interaction.
interpretationRequirements.IND-265: Distinguish a nominal micromolar inlet concentration from measured cellular exposure and transport through a particular interface.
interpretationRequirements.IND-276: Scope an inference to the physical and biological conditions a chip controls and the surrounding physiology it omits.
